blocks.content: The Vice-President shall be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States and shall not hold any other office of profit.

rows: Elected members of Parliament + Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi & Puducherry)
Elected AND Nominated members of Parliament only (No State Legislative Assemblies)
Must be qualified for election as a member of Lok Sabha
Must be qualified for election as a member of Rajya Sabha
Can be initiated in either House of Parliament
Can ONLY be initiated in the Rajya Sabha

items: Unlike Presidential elections, nominated members of Parliament CAN vote in the Vice-Presidential election.
Members of State Legislative Assemblies (MLAs) DO NOT participate in the Vice-Presidential election.
All doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a Vice-President are inquired into and decided exclusively by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final.
A formal impeachment is not required for the removal of the Vice-President, and the resolution can ONLY be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Vice-President occupies the second highest office in the country, modeled on the lines of the American Vice-President.
Acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and draws salary in that capacity.
Elected by an electoral college consisting of both elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament.
State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in the election or removal of the Vice-President.
Can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of Rajya Sabha (effective majority) and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
